recording.starts: partway, on what looks like the first onboarding screen: the first frame is the goal question "What do you need help with?" with an almost empty progress bar and no back button; any splash or launch screen before it is not captured
recording.after_paywall: "Try for $0.00" opens the App Store sheet, which is cancelled; closing the paywall brings up "A Gift from Rootd" (a no-charge 3-day pass) and "Welcome to Rootd Premium", then home, where a permanent "Get fully Rootd, free for 3 days" banner, locked Sleep items and a $2.99/month "Unlock Chat with Ron" add-on keep reopening paywalls.

strategy: Rootd sells relief through a relationship and a promise rather than through a diagnosis or a personalised plan. It opens with a one-tap need and an immediate science card (user figures plus a university logo), runs a quick self-check whose answers are never shown back, introduces Ron the mascot at the sign-up wall, and then spends the last twenty seconds before the paywall stacking commitments: a streak pledge, reminders framed as Ron's support, a care-for-Ron points loop, a signed pledge ("I commit to myself!") and a kind send-off. The emotional arc runs from distress named, to trust, to warmth, to self-obligation, so that "Try for $0.00" reads as keeping a promise already made to yourself. The idea that carries it is consistency: having promised, signed and been cheered on, saying no at the price feels like breaking your word to yourself.

phases.name: Hook and proof
phases.goal: Get the person to name their problem in one tap and believe straight away that the app works, using numbers and an institution, before anything personal is asked.

phases.name: Self-check
phases.goal: A fast, low-stakes self-assessment that makes the person register how they are doing and voice a wish to change, plus attribution and payer questions that serve the business. Nothing is reflected back, so it works on the person's own sense of readiness rather than on a sense of being analysed.

phases.name: Meet Ron, make an account
phases.goal: Turn the app into a relationship with a friendly character and get an account (an investment and a contact channel) while signalling scale and quality.

phases.name: Pledge and reminders
phases.goal: Convert the fresh account into a first-person habit promise and a reminder channel, with denial of notifications met by repeated nudges.

phases.name: Contract and send-off
phases.goal: Add an emotional obligation to Ron, seal the commitment with a drawn signature, then release the tension with kindness so the paywall reads as the first step of a promise already made.

phases.name: Paywall and win-back
phases.goal: Make starting an annual trial feel free, safe and already under way; when the person declines, hand them a no-charge pass so they enter the app as a "Premium" user who can be converted later.

screens.title: What do you need help with?
screens.controls: Options: Stop panic attacks; Manage anxiety; Learn to relax; Mood tracking; Improve sleep; OCD (single tap advances, no Continue button)
screens.visual: Pale blue sky and clouds, Ron (teal mascot) in glasses reading a book; white pill options with small icons (red brain, flower, open book, mood gauge, moon and cloud, orange pill). Progress bar almost empty with a yellow star at its end; no back button.
screens.intent: One tap to name the need, with the acute problem ("Stop panic attacks") listed first. Answering costs nothing and frames Rootd as the fix for that need from the first second.

screens.title: Rootd is backed by science
screens.body: 70% of users said mood improved after completing a single Rootd exercise / 50%+ users saw a decrease in their anxiety scores after using Rootd for 2 weeks / Average time of resolving a panic attack across 33,965 users 1 min 42 seconds / University of Victoria
screens.controls: Button: Good to know
screens.visual: Ron meditating cross-legged in front of a pink sun; three white bordered cards with the key phrases in bold ("70%", "mood improved", "50%+", "decrease in their anxiety", "Average time", "1 min 42 seconds"); University of Victoria crest and wordmark below; teal pill button. Bar slightly fuller than screen 1. Seen 0:01.3-0:05.3, and again 0:06.7-0:09.0 because the tester went back from screen 3 (reverse slide, bar drops back), then tapped Good to know a second time.
screens.intent: Placed after a single tap and before any personal question, it answers the anxious person's first doubt (will this work for me?) with precise-looking numbers and an institution, so the questionnaire feels like it leads somewhere proven. The figures are the app's own user metrics with no study or source named, and the university logo implies endorsement without saying what the university did; "Good to know" invites the person to accept the claims as fact.

screens.title: Have you tried anxiety exercises?
screens.controls: Options: Total beginner; I've done a little; I do them regularly (single tap advances)
screens.visual: Ron meditating in clouds; three white pills. Bar about a fifth full. Shown 0:05.7-0:06.7, then again 0:09.0-0:13.0 after the tester's back-and-forward.
screens.intent: Gauges experience; "Total beginner" listed first reassures newcomers that they are the expected user.

screens.title: How long do you usually sleep at night?

screens.intent: Two of three answers are written as a wish to change ("I'd like to improve", "I want to make some big changes"), so most people state a desire for change in their own voice, which the pledge screens later cash in.

screens.intent: Asks about self-discipline just before the habit and commitment screens; the low answer is phrased as asking for help and wanting to change, which sets up the streak pledge as the help.

screens.intent: Collects email and password, justified by future progress tracking. Making the account before the paywall adds sunk effort and gives the app a follow-up channel whatever happens at the price.

screens.title: Invest in yourself with a new daily habit
screens.body: Real progress starts with a promise, and Rootd works best with consistency. Choose your goal.
screens.controls: Options: I commit to a 7 day streak; I commit to a 10 day streak; I commit to a 14 day streak; I commit to a 30 day streak (single tap advances; which one was tapped is not visible)
screens.visual: Back to the sky-and-hills style with Ron meditating. The progress bar restarts almost empty here: a second section begins after sign-up and will fill to 100% at screen 20.
screens.intent: The first screen after sign-up turns the new account into a promise. Every option is a first-person commitment, no "not sure" or skip is shown, and the smallest pledge (7 days) is already longer than the 3-day free trial offered twenty seconds later, so keeping your word implies still using, and paying for, the app after the trial ends. A foot-in-the-door step that the signature and paywall build on.

screens.title: Get support from Ron
screens.body: Sample notification: You are strong and you are loved 💫 (now)
screens.controls: Continue; Maybe later
screens.visual: Bright green hills, Ron in glasses wearing a gold medal with arms raised, fireworks, confetti and stars; a white notification card with Ron's avatar. Bar about two fifths full.
screens.intent: Reframes a notification request as care from the mascot: the sample push is an affirmation, and the medal and confetti celebrate the person as if something has been achieved. Sitting right after the pledge, reminders read as the way to keep that promise, and the primary button says "Continue" rather than "Allow", so the OS prompt arrives as the result of simply moving on.

screens.title: “Rootd” Would Like to Send You Notifications
screens.body: Notifications may include alerts, sounds, and icon badges. These can be configured in Settings.
screens.controls: Don’t Allow; Allow
screens.visual: iOS alert over the dimmed primer, fired by Continue. The app's settings modal that follows suggests Don't Allow was tapped.
screens.intent: The system prompt the primer was built to set up; it appears only after the celebratory framing has done its work.

screens.title: Enable reminders
screens.body: To get this feature you'll need to turn on notifications in the app settings.
screens.controls: Turn On Notifications; X (close)
screens.visual: White modal over the darkened primer. Shown 0:59.7-1:00.7, closed, then shown again 1:01.7-1:02.7 when the primer is tapped a second time; the tester then moves on (the frames do not show which button did it).
screens.intent: After a clear no, the app pushes the person to Settings, and pressing the primer's main button again brings the same modal back, so the primary path keeps returning to the request; only closing it and finding the secondary route moves on. The copy frames the refusal as losing a feature.

screens.title: Take care of Ron
screens.body: Take care of Ron (and yourself) by completing simple daily self care goals, collecting points as you go (and grow) 🌱
screens.controls: Button: Continue
screens.visual: Ron in glasses reading his book in front of a pink sun, sky and waves; bar a little over half full. 1:04.0-1:07.3.
screens.intent: Introduces a pet-care loop: the person's self-care is framed as looking after Ron, with points as the reward. It adds a second, emotional obligation (a character who depends on you) on top of the streak and previews the daily return habit the subscription pays for.

screens.title: Ready to commit?
screens.body: Give yourself the best chance for anxiety relief by committing to Rootd. Sign below.
screens.controls: Signature pad with a reset icon. Button: I commit to myself!
screens.visual: Ron meditating in clouds; a large white signature box; the tester draws a scribbled signature from 1:08.5 to 1:10.0. Bar about four fifths full. No skip link is shown.
screens.intent: The strongest pressure point in the flow, two screens before the price. The person must draw a signature under a sentence that equates getting relief with "committing to Rootd", and the only button speaks in their voice ("I commit to myself!"), so continuing means performing the pledge. Signing a contract seconds before a paywall uses consistency pressure on an anxious audience: declining the trial next feels like breaking a promise to yourself. The paywall that follows then says "No commitment. Cancel anytime.", the opposite of the ritual it comes after.

screens.title: Wahoo, let's get started!
screens.body: Stick with Ron as you explore Rootd, learn to manage anxiety, and return calm to your life. Be patient and kind with yourself. / You got this.
screens.controls: Button: Continue
screens.visual: Ron lifting a barbell in a headband, stars bursting above him; the progress bar animates to completely full by 1:12.7, when the paywall slides up over this screen.
screens.intent: A warm release after the signature: permission to be imperfect, a full progress bar and a sense of the programme starting. It reads as the end of onboarding, so the paywall that rises over it feels like the first step of what was just promised rather than a sales screen. The kindness is genuine in tone but is also used to lower resistance at the moment of payment.

intermission_pattern: Rootd uses very few intermissions (4 in 20 pre-paywall screens) and puts them in two clusters rather than spacing them out. One proof card (science, screen 2) comes straight after the first tap, then eight questions run back to back with no reaction, mirroring, summary or loader at all; the answers are never shown back, so the questionnaire builds readiness to change rather than a sense of being analysed. Ron sits on every screen, so warmth comes from the mascot's poses (meditating, reading, waving, lifting weights) rather than from interstitial copy. After the account is made, the second progress section turns into a commitment ladder: a streak pledge (a question), a notification primer dressed as Ron's support, a care-for-Ron points explainer, a signed pledge and a kind send-off, each one screen long with one button. Tone is cheerful, cartoonish and kind throughout. Collectively they build toward an identity (someone who has promised to stick with Rootd and with Ron) rather than toward a personalised plan or result, and that identity is what the paywall's "Try for $0.00" asks the person to act on.
standouts: Screen 2 puts a science card with precise figures ("33,965 users", "1 min 42 seconds") and a University of Victoria logo after only one tap, borrowing institutional authority before asking anything personal, without naming a study or saying what the university's role was.
Screen 14's smallest pledge, "I commit to a 7 day streak", is longer than the 3-day free trial offered twenty seconds later, so keeping the promise quietly implies paying.

Screen 19 asks the person to draw a signature and tap "I commit to myself!" two screens before the price, and the paywall then reassures "No commitment. Cancel anytime.": the pressure is moved off the paywall and onto a self-promise ritual.

Screen 20 closes the commitment ladder with "Be patient and kind with yourself. You got this." while the progress bar fills to 100%, softening the person just as the paywall rises over the same screen.
gaps: The recording starts on the goal question with no back button and an almost empty bar, so it is probably the first onboarding screen, but any splash or launch screen is not shown. The science card appears twice only because the tester went back from screen 3 (reverse slide, bar drops back) and then forward again; it is one entry. Selected answers are not highlighted in any captured frame, so the options picked (including the streak length and the tracking prompt choice) are not visible; Don't Allow on the notification prompt is inferred from the settings modal that follows, and which button finally advanced past screen 17 is not visible. Screen 5 is missed by the contact sheets (they catch it only leaving at 0:18.3); its start time of about 0:16.0 comes from a 2 fps check of the video. A different welcome page (with an offline-help callout, an Editors' Choice laurel and Enter without account / Enter with account) flashes for about one frame at 0:35.3; it is described inside screen 12 rather than given its own entry. Screen 12 has six page dots but only the first page is shown. The typed email and the Apple account email on the purchase sheets are left out on purpose. The App Store sheets are folded into the paywall and app entries. counts.other = 2 account + 1 paywall + 2 exit + 3 app entries. The streak pledge (screen 14) is counted as a question because it is a picker; the signature (screen 19) is counted as an intermission because it collects no answer, only a ritual act. No new mechanism names were added.
